YouTube title seed: How Does a Torn QR Code Still Scan?
YouTube description seed: How much of a QR code can you rip off? Take a guess. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: QR codes store extra error-correction data so missing parts can be rebuilt; the three corner squares are only for locating the code.
The later surprise: At the highest error-correction level, about 30% of the code can be damaged and still be read.
The very first frame shows a printed QR code on paper with a corner torn off, a phone camera scanning it. Nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
Hook test: A (statement) = "Part of this QR code is torn off. It still scans."; B (question) = "How does a torn QR code still scan?".
Fact boundaries: Do not say any tear works; it depends on how much and where. Damage to the corner finder squares can stop it scanning. The main reveal lands in scene 4.

facts.statement: The three large squares in QR code corners are finder patterns that let a scanner locate and orient the code.
QR codes use Reed-Solomon error correction; level H can restore about 30% of damaged data.
